snp5.1:1.2: From the delightful city of the Kosalans to the Southern lands went
snp5.1:1.3: one who wanted to have no possessions, a brahmin perfect in the Vedas.
snp5.1:2.1: In the locality of Assaka, and near to Mūḷaka,
snp5.1:2.3: close to the bank of the Godhāvari he lived on gleanings and fruit.
snp5.1:3.1: In the vicinity (of the river) there was a large village,
snp5.1:3.4: and with the income that arose from that he offered a great sacrifice.
snp5.1:4.1: When that great sacrifice had been given he entered his hermitage again,
snp5.1:4.4: and when he had re-entered it, another brahmin came along -
snp5.1:5.2: he had sore feet, and was thirsty, with dirty teeth, and dust on his head -
snp5.1:5.3: and after approaching (the first brahmin), he begged for five hundred (coins).
snp5.1:6.1: After seeing him Bāvari invited him to take a seat,
snp5.1:6.3: and he asked after his happiness and welfare, and this is the word he spoke:
snp5.1:7.1: “Whatever kind of gift I had, all that has been given away by me,
snp5.1:7.4: please excuse me brahmin, I do not have the five hundred.”
snp5.1:8.2: “If your honour will not give me what I am begging for,
snp5.1:8.4: then within seven days may your head split into seven pieces!”
snp5.1:9.1: Having made (a scene) the dishonest man proclaimed this fearful thing.
snp5.1:9.3: After hearing this word of his, Bāvari became miserable.
snp5.1:10.2: (Going) without food he dried up, and was affected by the dart of grief,
snp5.1:10.3: and when his heart was like that his mind did not delight in meditation.
snp5.1:11.1: Having seen him terrified and miserable, a God who desired his welfare,
snp5.1:11.3: approached Bāvari, and this is the word he spoke:
snp5.1:12.1: “He does not know the head - he is a dishonest man who wants wealth!
snp5.1:12.4: He does not have knowledge about the head or head-splitting.”
snp5.1:13.2: “But now your honour knows! Please explain this to me when asked:
snp5.1:13.3: the head and head-splitting, may we hear that word of yours.”
snp5.1:14.1: “I also do not know about this, I do not have this knowledge here.
snp5.1:14.4: The head and head-splitting! Indeed only Victors see this!”
snp5.1:15.1: “Then who knows about the head and head-splitting
snp5.1:15.3: on the face of the earth? O God, please explain this to me.”
snp5.1:16.1: “From out of the city of Kapilavatthu a world leader has renounced,
snp5.1:16.4: he is of king Okkāka’s line, a Sakyan’s son, a Light-Maker.
snp5.1:17.1: He is a Sambuddha, brahmin, in everything he is perfect,
snp5.1:17.3: having attained all deep knowledges and strengths, endowed with Vision regarding all things,
snp5.1:17.6: he has come to the end of all actions, in the end of all clinging he is freed.
snp5.1:18.2: He is the Buddha in the world, the Fortunate One, the Visionary who teaches Teaching,
snp5.1:18.3: after going there you can ask him about it, he will explain it to you.”
snp5.1:19.1: Having heard the word ‘Sambuddha’, Bāvari became elated,
snp5.1:19.4: then his grief became but little, and he received great happiness.
snp5.1:20.3: “In which village, or again in which town,
snp5.1:20.4: in which country, is the lord of the world?
snp5.1:20.6: Where having gone to can we revere the Sambuddha, the Supreme Human Being?”
snp5.1:21.1: “The Victor is in the Kosalan’s city, Sāvatthī,
snp5.1:21.2: he has much wisdom, excellent and great intelligence,
snp5.1:21.3: that Sakyan’s son, who is free from burden and pollutant,
snp5.1:21.4: that Bull of a Man has understanding of head-splitting.”
snp5.1:22.1: So then the brahmin addressed his students, who were perfect in the the Vedas:
snp5.1:22.3: “Come, young men, and I shall explain, please listen to this word of mine:
snp5.1:23.1: He whose manifestation in the world is always exceptional,
snp5.1:23.4: has now arisen in the world, renowned as one called a ‘Sambuddha’.
snp5.1:23.5: Having gone quickly to Sāvatthī, you can see the Supreme Human Being.”
snp5.1:24.2: “Having seen him how will we know that he is the ‘Buddha’, O brahmin?
snp5.1:24.4: You must tell us who do not know, how we can know it is him.”
snp5.1:25.2: “There has come down to us in the the Vedas the marks of a Great Man,
snp5.1:25.4: they are explained as thirty-two, complete in regular order.
snp5.1:26.1: For whoever has on his limbs the marks of a Great Man,
snp5.1:26.3: there can be just two destinies, for a third cannot be found:
snp5.1:27.1: If he lives in a house, when he has been victorious over this earth,
snp5.1:27.4: without a stick or a sword he will rule according to the Teaching.
snp5.1:28.1: But if he goes forth from the house to the houseless life,
snp5.1:28.3: he becomes a Cover-Remover, a Sambuddha, a Worthy One, unexcelled.
snp5.1:29.1: About my birth, family, and marks; lore, students and other things,
snp5.1:29.3: about the head and head-splitting, you must ask in your mind.
snp5.1:30.2: If he should be a Buddha, one who sees without obstruction,
snp5.1:30.3: the questions that are asked in your mind he will answer by way of speech.”
snp5.1:31.2: After hearing Bāvari’s words, the sixteen brahmin students:
snp5.1:31.3: Ajita, Tissa Metteyya, Puṇṇaka, also Mettagū,
snp5.1:32.2: Dhotaka, and Upasīva, Nanda, and also Hemaka,
snp5.1:32.3: the two: Todeyya and Kappa, and Jatukaṇṇī, the one who is wise,
snp5.1:33.1: Bhadrāvudha and Udaya, and also the brahmin Posāla,
snp5.1:33.3: Mogharāja, the intelligent one, and the great seer, Piṅgiya,
snp5.1:34.2: each one with his own group, renowned throughout the whole world,
snp5.1:34.3: meditators delighting in meditation, wise ones, influenced by their pre-dispositions,
snp5.1:35.2: after worshipping Bāvari, and circumambulating him,
snp5.1:35.4: they all, wearing matted-hair and deer-skins, set out for the North:
snp5.1:36.1: From Mūḷaka to Patiṭṭhāna first, then on to Mahissati,
snp5.1:36.3: to Ujjenī, and Gonaddha, to Vedisa, and to the place called Vanasa,
snp5.1:37.2: to Kosambī, and Sāketa, and Sāvatthī, the city supreme,
snp5.1:37.3: to Setabya, and Kapilavatthu, and to the city of Kusinārā,
snp5.1:38.2: to Pāvā, to Bhoganagara, to Vesālī, and to the Magadhan city (Rājagaha),
snp5.1:38.4: and to the Pāsāṇaka shrine, delightful, it is the mind’s delight.
snp5.1:39.1: Just like a thirsty man to cool water, or like a trader to great gain,
snp5.1:39.3: like one scorched by the heat to shade, quickly he climbed the mountain.
snp5.1:40.2: Now at that time the Fortunate One was in front of the community of monks,
snp5.1:40.3: teaching the Teaching to the monks, roaring like a lion in a forest,
snp5.1:41.2: Ajita saw the Sambuddha, brilliant like the hundred-rayed sun,
snp5.1:41.3: like the moon which has reached fullness on the fifteenth day of the month,
snp5.1:42.2: and after seeing on his limbs the characteristics in their fullness,
snp5.1:42.3: standing cheerfully on one side he asked a question in his mind:
snp5.1:43.2: “Speak and point out his birth, speak of his family, and marks,
snp5.1:43.3: speak of his perfection in the Vedas, how many does the brahmin school?”
snp5.1:44.1: “One hundred and twenty years his age, his family is Bāvari,
snp5.1:44.4: three marks are on his limbs, he is perfect in the three Vedas.
snp5.1:45.2: In the marks, and the traditions, with the glossaries, and the ritual,
snp5.1:45.4: he schools five hundred, in his own teaching he is perfect.”
snp5.1:46.1: “(Your) investigation of Bāvari’s marks, O One Supreme among Men,
snp5.1:46.3: O craving-cutter, make that clear, so that we are not left doubting.”
snp5.1:47.1: “He can cover his face with his tongue, there is hair between his eyebrows,
snp5.1:47.3: what is covered by a cloth is ensheathed: know it is so young man.”
snp5.1:48.1: Not hearing any question, but having heard the questions answered,
snp5.1:48.3: all the people were enthusiastic, and raised their hands, thinking:
snp5.1:49.2: “Now who was it, a God, or a Brahma, or Inda, the lord of Sujā,
snp5.1:49.3: who asked those questions with the mind? To whom did he make reply?
snp5.1:50.1: “About the head and head-splitting, Bāvari asks (this question),
snp5.1:50.3: please explain that O Fortunate One, please remove our doubts, O seer.”
snp5.1:51.1: "Know ignorance is called the head, and understanding is the head-splitter,
snp5.1:51.4: joined with confidence, mindfulness, concentration, desire, and energy.”
snp5.1:52.2: Then with great enthusiasm, being resolute, the young man,
snp5.1:52.3: having put his deer-skin on one shoulder, fell placing his head at (the Buddha’s) feet:
snp5.1:53.1: “The honourable brahmin Bāvari, and his students, dear Sir,
snp5.1:53.4: elated in heart, and happy in mind, worships your feet, O Visionary One.”
snp5.1:54.2: “May the brahmin Bāvari, together with his students, be happy!
snp5.1:54.3: And may you also be happy! May you live for a long time, young man!
snp5.1:55.2: All of the doubts that Bāvari, or you, or anyone else has,
snp5.1:55.4: having received leave, ask whatever you long (to know) in the mind.”
snp5.1:56.1: Having received leave from the Sambuddha, sitting with hands raised in reverence,
snp5.1:56.4: Ajita asked the Realised One the first question in that place:
